shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The psalm closes with an imperative petition for the city, “Do well in your good pleasure to Zion. Build the walls of Jerusalem.” (web:Ps.51.18), where OSHB names צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה — ‘Zion—you will build’ (oshb:Ps.51.20) — and resolves in “Then you will delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt offerings and in whole burnt offerings. Then they will offer bulls on your altar.” (web:Ps.51.19). The topographic naming of Zion and Jerusalem's walls, absent from the rest of the psalm, marks this as a distinct closing unit.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 51:18-19 as continuous with 51:13-17 rather than a separate unit is the mandated rival: commentators disagree on whether the Zion petition is integral to the psalm or a later liturgical addition responding to Jerusalem's walls being broken, since the verse names actual city walls rather than speaking figuratively of the individual penitent. The candidate holds it as its own unit given its topographic register shift (see observed_substrate_signals), but the seam is registered as uncertain.
observed_substrate_signals: oshb:Ps.51.20 (web:Ps.51.18) is the sole occurrence in the psalm of צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה (‘Zion—you will build’; sweep: 1 verse); the standalone lexeme צִיּ֑וֹן (Zion) likewise occurs only here in the psalm (sweep: 1 verse)
shipped_row.device_notes: Closing Zion petition; a debated seam (see rejected_alternative) held here as its own low-confidence unit.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The psalmist's voice turns from petition to vow, “Then I will teach transgressors your ways. Sinners will be converted to you.” (web:Ps.51.13), where OSHB's אֲלַמְּדָ֣ה (“I will teach”, a 1cs cohortative with paragogic he, oshb:Ps.51.15) opens the verse, and moves through the plea “Deliver me from the guilt of bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation. My tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness.” (web:Ps.51.14) and “Lord, open my lips. My mouth will declare your praise.” (web:Ps.51.15) into a theological claim about sacrifice, “For you don't delight in sacrifice, or else I would give it. You have no pleasure in burnt offering.” (web:Ps.51.16), closing “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.” (web:Ps.51.17). This unit's cohortative-vow opening and its sacrifice-theology close both mark it off from the imperative cluster before it and the Zion petition after it.
